topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, outlines the lecture series, and introduces the key learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer: Genetic Mutations, Environmental Exposures, and Epidemiological Patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer develops from an interplay of intrinsic genetic processes, random mutations, environmental exposures, and lifestyle factors demonstrated through population epidemiology.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how infectious agents contribute to oncogenesis, using the relationship between Epstein-Barr virus, malaria, and Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed case study.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which dietary, environmental, and chemical agents undergo metabolic processing to cause DNA damage and adduct formation.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Context-Dependent Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, contrasting tumor promoters and chronic inflammation with initiators and highlighting tissue- and developmental-stage vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Evaluating Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the laboratory, genomic, in vivo, and epidemiological approaches used to identify mutational signatures and assess the carcinogenic potential of chemical agents.

topics.label: Conclusion and Everyday Risk Assessment
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by summarising key takeaways regarding environmental carcinogens and reflecting on daily risk-benefit decisions.
